## Open

### T-127 — Implement the planned adapter idle handling

> _2026-09-22 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Planned feature, not a defect (reworded from S20 at the maintainer request: keep the names, present
them as future work). patterns/handler.md documents idleSend, idleReceive and drainSend as the
intended lifecycle hooks for keep-alive and idle handling, and the page now marks them as planned
rather than current while saying which configuration is already written for them. To implement:
dispatch the three hooks from the adapter loop (idle after a configured quiet period on the send and
the receive side, drain when the send queue empties), read the idleSend and idleReceive
configuration keys that concepts/adapter.md:35, patterns/adapter.md and
test/framework/ctp/adapter/payshield.ts:10 already set, and give AdapterBase.drain, which is
subscribed to the drain event, real behaviour.

### T-142 — blong-gogo graceful shutdown test fails on its own

> _2026-09-24 · core/blong-gogo · open_

src/graceful-shutdown.spawn.test.ts fails with the CLI exiting 143 rather than 0, both in a full run
and when run alone, while the rest of the suite is green. Nothing in this session touched the CLI or
its shutdown path, so it looks pre-existing and environment-dependent: check whether the marker file
is flushed before the signal is delivered, and whether a loaded machine is enough to lose the race,
before changing the code.

### T-153 — Teach the browser guards about modules the loader imports dynamically

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-gogo · open_

core/blong-gogo/scripts/browser-compat-check.mjs (node --run browser-check) is the only check that
catches a module a dev server cannot link, since it starts a dev server, opens Chromium and fails on
any console error, but nothing runs it and it needs Chromium. Wire it into CI for one suite, or
extend core/blong-browser/src/browserBundle.test.ts with a development-mode build so the modules the
loader imports dynamically become part of the graph it inspects — a static import inside one of them
breaks the page in dev while a production bundle stays silent. The source scan in
core/blong-gogo/src/browserEagerImports.test.ts covers the chain only; other node-only modules
belong in its NODE_ONLY list once they are known.

### T-154 — The slow-step margin does not reach the registry's start steps

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-gogo · open_

`log.slowMs` tunes the loader's steps and the retention store, and a runner may raise it for a
machine that is legitimately slow, but two callers of `withProgress` ignore it. `Registry.ts` passes
`getProgress` only for `create ports`, `start ports`, `ready ports` and `stop ports`, and
`core/blong-gogo/src/adapter/server/knex.ts`'s `ready` does the same for `schema table sync` and the
constraint pass, so all of them keep the compiled default of 1000ms and raising the margin cannot
silence them. If a slow startup ever warns under one of those labels, this is why. Give those calls
the configured margin — check first what the registry's `#config` carries, since the `log` block is
a platform-level sibling rather than part of the registry's section, while the knex adapter has the
same reach to `this.config`.

### T-183 — Log the gateway's effective port whether or not it was configured

> _2026-09-30 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Gateway.ts only speaks about the port when it was chosen at random, and only as a warn that is
suppressed at logLevel info and above: a statically configured port is never logged, and a random
one is silent in dev. Starting a gateway for the Storybook live modes therefore leaves an agent to
poll ss for a port it cannot be told about, and a server-only entry (gateway.port 0) gives no clue
either way. Emit the effective port once at startup — the configured value and the bound value — at
a level that survives the dev intent's log level.

### T-195 — Five helper modules still log a load error in their group folders

> _2026-10-04 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The loader gives every file in a handler group the shape of a handler and logs an error-level line
for a module that is not one. Five predate this: gatewayUuid.ts (blong-gateway adapter/db), core.ts
(blong-core adapter/db), oidc.ts, account.ts and accessModel.ts (blong-access adapter/db). Each run
prints Watch error loading X probably a generic source code was put in a handler group folder, which
is five error-level entries every suite run and trains a reader to ignore the stream that expected
errors were just cleaned up. Either the loader should skip a module that exports no handler and no
library, or those files should become libraries.

### T-217 — Warn when a CLI config key matches no realm, port or framework key

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

A config override addressed one level too shallow is dropped in silence, which cost a long
investigation (F-370). The loader merges argv into the runtime config and then hands each port only
`mergedConfig[realm][port]`, so any key outside that slice is invisible: no validation error and no
log line. Emit a warning (or at least a debug log) when `--x.y=z` matches no realm, port or
framework key, so the next author sees the mistake in the first run instead of concluding that
config overrides do not work.

### T-225 — A watch reply arrives empty across the request boundary

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

The cluster adapter watch verb answers {events: asyncGenerator, existing} and what reaches the
controller carries neither key: a probe logged no existing and no stream, on a watch that opened
successfully and repeated once a second at the pacing floor.

Now explained: the whole reply is dropped, not the stream within it, and only on the path that
crosses a transport — the deploy port's request call. A handler reaches the same adapter through the
in-process proxy and receives both the initial list and the generator intact (see T-227 for the
probe). That is why a watch opened correctly and delivered nothing: the adapter was fine, and the
values were gone before the controller saw them. The realm therefore runs its watch from a handler,
and the resync interval is no longer the only trigger that works.

### T-228 — The k8s adapter's list answer carries no kind or apiVersion

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

A find answer here holds only metadata, spec and status on each item, while the API server returns
kind and apiVersion per item as well. Every caller therefore has to know the type from its own
request, which is what the kustomize diff had to be taught to do after it read eighteen objects as
obsolete beside eighteen creations (T-226).

Decide whether the adapter should keep the type identity the server sent, or whether a list is
documented as type-blind, and say so in the adapter so the next consumer does not rediscover it.
Worth checking first whether the loss is in the client library turning the response into objects
rather than in the adapter, since the same reply feeds the explorer and the deployment UI.

### T-250 — An unreachable database can kill a process by event

> _2026-10-06 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Found while fixing T-235 and not fixed with it. The knex adapter's start wraps ensureDatabase in
try/catch and warns, and the intent is plainly to continue: schema sync will surface the real
failure. What actually happened when the host did not resolve was a process-ending error with a
stack of one frame (getaddrinfo) and no await above it, which is the shape of an unhandled error
event on the mysql2 connection rather than a rejected promise the catch could see. Confirm it by
pointing a dev run at a name that does not resolve with the old code path, then make the failure
arrive through the caller: attach an error listener the moment the connection exists, or let
ensureDatabase reject in a way that does not also emit. It matters because a warn-and-continue that
kills the process is worse than a throw, which at least says where it came from.

### T-272 — The pino implementation callSite path is unverified

> _2026-10-07 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Log.ts wraps the level methods of every logger it hands out when log.callSite is configured, yet a

### T-227 — The adapter replies null for a watch, and the generator dies there

> _2026-10-05 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Probed at the call site: cluster.custom.watch answers the packet
`[null, {mtid: response, method: cluster.custom.watch}]`, while cluster.custom.find answers real
data with the same coordinates, so the routing, the resource type and the group/version/plural are
all right and only the watch reply loses its value. The adapter carries no codec, so this is not a
wire encoding step, and it is not the meta wrapping either: what is left is the reply path around
the adapter handler.

Characterised on the second attempt. The loss is not in the adapter and not in the generator: a call
that reaches the adapter through a handler proxy carries the stream whole, and the realm's
kustomize.watch.run now logs "watch: open with 1 existing, stream present" and reconciles from the
list it receives. The call the port makes, through the deploy port's request path, is the one that
answers null. So the defect to fix is narrower than "a reply cannot carry a stream": a reply that
cannot be carried is replaced by a null instead of raising, and the caller cannot tell a dropped
result from an empty one. Fix the silence first (the reply path should refuse a value it cannot
carry), then decide whether the transport should carry the generator rather than only data.

### T-285 — The intents fixture ignores the config it is handed

> _2026-10-09 · core/blong-gogo · open_

Fixing the unused-variable lint error in frameworkRealms.test.ts meant renaming a parameter, not
reading it: the helper is
`withConfig = (url, config) => server(() => ({url, children: [], config: {default: {}}}))`, so every
case that builds a different config hands it to a mock that serves a fixed `{default: {}}` and
ignores the argument. The parameter was named `config` and unused, which is exactly what a reader
notices as a smell and a lint rule as an error; it is now `_config` and the smell is gone from the
report but not from the test. Worth checking whether the cases differ only in what they pass (in
which case the mock should serve it) or whether the shared fixture is the point and the parameter
can go.

### T-286 — Nothing runs the Dockerfile manifests check

> _2026-10-10 · core/blong-gogo · open_

`core/blong-gogo/docker/manifests.mjs --check` fails when the generated COPY block in
`blong-gogo.Dockerfile` is stale, and its own comment says CI runs it, but nothing does: the block
had lost the `test/blong-int-kustomize` package manifest and the Kustomize E2E workflow died in the
image build (2m33s) because `rush install` inside the image named a project with no manifest. Wire
the check into the lint job, which needs no cluster, so the next package cannot break the image
silently.
